title: Bridge signed-query suspension and return on 23 fixed tapes
body:
The retained signed-query routine and continuation stack use different tape alphabets, and the existing output-return routine requires an empty parent destination while the query's Z is occupied. This package supplies the paid representation and return connection: the actual 243/248-instruction query tables now suspend and resume on the same 23 physical tapes at every finite nesting depth, under explicit signed-range and input-format conditions.

The proof includes internal logical blanks, staging, restoration of parent counters, output protection before destructive pop, installation into the occupied Z, and retained backing. It derives the exact additional boundary charge `34Lz + 21Lp + 21Lm + 13L + 283`. Independent review caught a coded-blank-tail counterexample to an overly broad space corollary; the corrected hypothesis and exact scaling diagnostic are included.

The same package independently binds the current PR5811 complex raw ownership grammar (626 safe private banks) and retained PR4440 BIT grammar (129 safe private banks). A conditional allocation theorem and compiler name proof isolate the remaining application gap: the delayed-cover BIT's variable fiber/row interface and old atom-interchange space binding. **All five project assumptions remain retained; κ is unchanged.** The implemented unary-depth test grammar uses a named identity leaf; actual production dispatch, child numerics and global precision remain open.

Validation: normal and isolated optimized registered replay, 114 nested chains, nine unequal subjobs, 27 exact invoices, eight coded-tail cases, physical/ownership/name mutations, and source-authenticated Git-free read-only export. See `VALIDATION.json` and `REVIEW.json` for exact scope. No complete multiplier or human/kernel acceptance is claimed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-owned-dispatch`.

Takes part of the released [Discussion5009 handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5009#discussioncomment-19172867); [canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5009#discussioncomment-19206017). Reuses PR5116, PR5356, PR5368, PR5404 and PR5443, with predecessor notices and exact pins retained. Mason Hale with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Only the new scoped research package is changed.
